sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Testing questions separate candidates who just know syntax from candidates who write maintainable code. At fresher level you don't need to know pytest fixtures deeply — you need to write a working test, explain why mocking exists, and name the test pyramid.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
**Test pyramid (from most to fewest):**

```
         /\ E2E (few)
        /  \
       / Int \ (moderate)
      /________\
     / Unit Tests \ (many)
    /______________\
```

Unit tests are fast, isolated, and cheap. E2E tests are slow, brittle, and expensive.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **Unit test** — tests one function/class in isolation. External dependencies (DB, API) are mocked.
- **pytest discovery** — files named `test_*.py` or `*_test.py`, functions starting with `test_`.
- **`assert` in pytest** — plain `assert x == y`. pytest rewrites it for helpful failure messages.
- **unittest.TestCase** — `setUp()`/`tearDown()` for setup/cleanup. `self.assertEqual()`, `self.assertRaises()`.
- **Mocking** — `unittest.mock.MagicMock` replaces real objects. `patch('module.function')` as decorator or context manager.
- **Why mock?** — tests run without a real database or network; fast and deterministic.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **'What is the difference between a unit test and an integration test?'** — unit test isolates one unit; integration test tests multiple components together.
- **'What is mocking?'** — replacing a real dependency (database, API) with a fake during tests so the test is fast and isolated.
- **'How does pytest find tests?'** — files matching `test_*.py`, functions starting with `test_`.
- **'What would you test for a login function?'** — valid credentials succeed, invalid credentials fail, account locked after N attempts, empty input handled.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I write unit tests for business logic and mock external dependencies like databases and APIs. pytest is my preference — less boilerplate than unittest and better failure messages. For a login function I'd test the happy path, wrong password, non-existent user, and empty input. I think about what can go wrong, not just what should work."*
